newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan Tamil rebels report refugee exodus.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan Tamil rebels report refugee exodus.

text.p: Sri Lanka's Tamil Tiger rebels on Sunday reported a mass exodus of refugees from villages in the path of the army's latest offensive in the island's northwest.

"Another humanitarian crisis is looming as Sri Lankan forces shell and (bomb) Tamil border villages on the edges of Vavuniya and Mannar districts," the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) said in a statement.
"Heavy artillery fire is raining down on a number of villages causing civilians to flee in massive waves," it said.

A defence ministry spokesman said he had no immediate information on the report but other military officials said previous army offensives against the rebels have caused similiar flows of refugees fleeing the fighting.
Government troops, backed by tanks, artillery and air support, are currently advancing into rebel territory in the northwestern Mannar region.

Troops, led by elite special forces and airmobile units, had advanced 22 km (14 miles) west of the frontline town of Vavuniya, 220 km (135 miles) north of Colombo, by Friday, the Defence Ministry said.
The rebels have avoided battle so far but launched an artillery strike with captured long-range guns on Vavuniya early on Saturday, killing two policemen in their barracks.
It was the first use of long-range artillery by the Tigers on Vavuniya, a strategic town from where government forces last Tuesday launched their biggest offensive so far this year.
The government immediately responded to the LTTE battery with an attack by helicopters and air force bombers.
The LTTE, fighting for a separate homeland for minority Tamils in this predominantly Sinhalese nation, appear to have been aiming at police and army barracks, residents said.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the 14-year old conflict. The LTTE says the toll is much higher.
